chapters.title: First Steps
chapters.blurb: One gradient. Read the ends, fill the middle.

chapters.title: Two Strokes
chapters.blurb: Two gradients at a time, and cells they share.

chapters.title: Crossings
chapters.blurb: Shapes built from strokes that cross.

chapters.title: Everyday Things
chapters.blurb: Bigger objects, more gradients, tighter steps.

chapters.title: Creatures
chapters.blurb: Chroma joins in. Neighbors start to look alike.

chapters.title: Landmarks
chapters.blurb: Wide scenes with long ramps to keep straight.

chapters.title: Mastery
chapters.blurb: Everything at once, with barely any given cells.

chapters.title: Workshop
chapters.blurb: Tools built from connected runs and shared joints.

chapters.title: Orchestra
chapters.blurb: Instruments with more parts to sort and align.

chapters.title: Circuitry
chapters.blurb: Dense networks where each crossing carries information.

chapters.title: Interiors
chapters.blurb: Rooms and structures assembled one section at a time.

chapters.title: Grand Works
chapters.blurb: Large machines and landmarks at the campaign's limit.

levels.name: Bar
levels.tip: Drag the swatch into the empty cell. Both ends are already placed.

levels.name: Post
levels.tip: Gradients run down as well as across.

levels.name: Beam
levels.tip: A longer run, same idea: even steps from one end to the other.

levels.name: Tower
levels.tip: The ends are given. Every cell between them is one step from the next.

levels.name: Spine
levels.tip: Long ramps step gently. Trust the ends.

levels.name: Domino
levels.tip: Two gradients now. They are different color families on purpose.

levels.name: Corner
levels.tip: Two strokes, one bend. Each stroke ramps on its own.

levels.name: Tee
levels.tip: Where the strokes meet, one cell belongs to both: one color doing two jobs.

levels.name: Cross
levels.tip: Solve the easier stroke first, then use the shared cell.

levels.name: Track
levels.tip: Neighbors. Check which row a swatch belongs to before dropping it.

levels.name: Goalpost
levels.tip: A stroke pinned at both ends has nothing left to guess.

levels.name: Frame
levels.tip: Every corner is shared. Work around the loop.

levels.name: Rake
levels.tip: Five gradients. The long one holds the other four in place.

levels.name: House
levels.tip: Bigger boards now. Place what you are sure of and the rest narrows.

levels.name: Train
levels.tip: The two long rows are the same length. Read left to right, not up and down.

levels.name: Fish
levels.tip: Chroma ramps now too: same hue, draining color.

levels.name: Snake
levels.tip: A chain of pinned strokes. Each one hands the next its start.

levels.name: Pyramid
levels.tip: Four parallel ramps, four families. Nothing crosses, nothing helps.

levels.name: Cascade
levels.tip: Nothing here is loose: every stroke shares an end with another one.

levels.name: Loom
levels.tip: Every crossing is a fact about two gradients at once.

levels.name: Mandala
levels.tip: Last one. Nine rows, six ramps, every crossing earning its keep.

levels.name: Screwdriver
levels.tip: Place the longest run first, then work outward from the cells it fixes.

levels.name: Toolbox
levels.tip: When a run carries more than one shared cell, settle that run before the ones hanging off it.

levels.name: Caliper
levels.tip: Eight ramps is a lot to hold at once, so finish one corner of the board completely before moving on.

levels.name: Metronome
levels.tip: Two runs span the whole board. Pin those and the short ones have nowhere left to go.

levels.name: Microphone
levels.tip: Pick a crossing and settle both runs through it before moving on.

levels.name: Violin Case
levels.tip: With this many ramps in play, finish one completely before you start the next.

levels.name: Antenna
levels.tip: Every crossing belongs to two runs at once. Solve one and you have solved a cell in both.

levels.name: Resistor
levels.tip: When one placement forces a neighbor, follow that chain as far as it goes before starting somewhere new.

levels.name: Microchip
levels.tip: Leave the short runs for last, once the long ones have pinned their neighbors.

levels.name: Refinery
levels.tip: The widest run reaches almost every vertical. Place it and the rest lose most of their freedom.

levels.name: Engine Shed
levels.tip: Where two runs meet, the shared cell has to satisfy both, so let it steer the pair.

levels.name: Ironworks
levels.tip: Two hundred boards. Take this one slowly, and finish it the way you like.
